smiles_audit.name: ethanol
smiles_audit.reason: Two-carbon chain ending in an implicit O-H group: CH3CH2OH.

smiles_audit.name: acetic acid
smiles_audit.reason: Methyl group attached to a carboxylic acid group: CH3COOH.

smiles_audit.name: ethyl acetate
smiles_audit.reason: Ethoxy group attached through oxygen to an acetyl group: CH3COOCH2CH3.

smiles_audit.name: benzaldehyde
smiles_audit.reason: The carbonyl carbon bears an implicit hydrogen and is directly attached to a benzene ring.

smiles_audit.name: toluene
smiles_audit.reason: A methyl group is attached to a benzene ring.

smiles_audit.name: acetone
smiles_audit.reason: The carbonyl carbon lies between two methyl groups: CH3COCH3.

smiles_audit.name: aniline
smiles_audit.reason: Neutral nitrogen has two implicit hydrogens and is directly attached to benzene: C6H5NH2.

smiles_audit.name: phenol
smiles_audit.reason: An O-H group is directly attached to an aromatic carbon.

smiles_audit.name: 1-bromobutane
smiles_audit.reason: An unbranched four-carbon chain has bromine on a terminal carbon.

smiles_audit.name: cyclohexene
smiles_audit.reason: A six-carbon ring contains exactly one carbon-carbon double bond.

smiles_audit.name: acetyl chloride
smiles_audit.reason: Chlorine is directly bonded to the acetyl carbonyl carbon: CH3COCl.

smiles_audit.name: nitrobenzene
smiles_audit.reason: A correctly charge-separated nitro group is attached to benzene through nitrogen.

smiles_audit.name: propan-1-ol
smiles_audit.reason: An unbranched three-carbon chain ends in CH2OH.

smiles_audit.name: propan-2-ol
smiles_audit.reason: The O-H group is attached to the central carbon of a three-carbon skeleton.

smiles_audit.name: propanal
smiles_audit.reason: The terminal carbonyl carbon bears an implicit hydrogen: CH3CH2CHO.

smiles_audit.name: propanoic acid
smiles_audit.reason: An ethyl group is attached to a carboxylic acid carbon, giving three carbons overall.

smiles_audit.name: butan-2-one
smiles_audit.reason: The carbonyl carbon is bonded to ethyl and methyl groups; numbering gives position 2.

first_carbonyl_then_hydroxyl.if: A strong C=O absorption is present at approximately 1650-1800 cm^-1; also inspect just above 1800 for an acyl chloride.

then.if: A very broad O-H envelope spans approximately 2500-3300 cm^-1 and overlaps the C-H region.
then.then: A carboxylic acid is strongly supported. Record both O-H and C=O.

else.if: A broad alcohol/phenol-like O-H band occurs near 3300 cm^-1 without swamping 2500 cm^-1.
else.then: Record both hydroxyl and carbonyl functionality. This is not a carbonyl-only compound; consider a hydroxy-carbonyl structure.

else.if: A weak aldehydic C-H feature occurs near 2720 cm^-1, possibly accompanied by another near 2820 cm^-1.
else.then: An aldehyde is supported; confirm with other information, especially a 1H NMR signal near 9-10 ppm.
else.else: A carbonyl group is established, but its class is not settled. Consider ketone, ester, aldehyde, amide or acyl chloride using position, supporting bands and other spectra.

else.if: A broad O-H band occurs near 3300 cm^-1 and does not extend strongly through 2500 cm^-1.
else.then: An alcohol or phenol is supported; distinguish them using aromatic evidence and other spectra.

else.if: An acid-like, very broad 2500-3300 cm^-1 envelope appears despite no clear C=O.
else.then: Recheck the carbonyl region and assignments. Do not confirm a carboxylic acid from broad O-H alone.
else.else: No O-H is established. Narrower N-H or terminal alkyne C-H bands near this region must not be relabelled automatically as O-H.

next_independently.if: A sharp absorption near 2250 cm^-1 is consistent with C≡N.
next_independently.then: Record a nitrile group in addition to any previously identified groups.
next_independently.else: No nitrile is established; continue without inventing a band.

finally_support.if: C-O absorption at 1300-1000 cm^-1 or recognizable fingerprint bands support the proposed structure.
finally_support.then: Use these as corroboration: aromatic C-H out-of-plane at 900-675, alkene C-H out-of-plane at 1000-650, and C-Cl at 800-600 cm^-1. Do not let them override contradictory diagnostic evidence.
finally_support.else: Keep the conclusion at the functional-group level supported by the diagnostic regions; use MS and NMR to resolve ambiguity.

ir_rules.note: Hydrogen-bonded alcohol template. Broad, but not an acid-like envelope extending strongly to 2500. Width is an approximate FWHM in cm^-1; depth_pct is the downward percentage-point excursion from a 100% transmittance baseline. All values are schematic defaults, not fitted measurements.
Phenolic O-H can resemble alcoholic O-H. Use aromatic and aryl C-O evidence for support.

Draw a continuous broad envelope overlapping alkyl C-H, not merely an alcohol-shaped band at 3300. Use smoothly limited tails, roughly 2400-3500, so the envelope does not create false carbonyl-region absorption.
One of two N-H stretching bands for a primary amine, including aniline. Flag excludes amides; actual positions depend on environment.
Second member of the NH2 pair; these bands are normally much narrower than the hydrogen-bonded alcohol O-H envelope.
Applies to acetone and butan-2-one. A separate hydroxyl elsewhere in the molecule does not suppress this rule.
Conjugation usually lowers the ketone C=O frequency. Mutually exclusive with the saturated-ketone rule for the same carbonyl.
Applies to propanal. Carbonyl position alone is not a secure aldehyde-versus-ketone test.
Applies to benzaldehyde, whose carbonyl is conjugated directly with the aromatic ring.
Applies to ethyl acetate. Include supporting C-O absorption and no O-H unless a separate hydroxyl group exists.
Applies to acetic and propanoic acids in a hydrogen-bonded condensed-phase template. Must accompany the acid O-H envelope.
Applies to acetyl chloride. Do not restrict carbonyl detection to frequencies strictly below 1800.
Supporting rule for carbonyl classification beyond the audited list. Amide N-H must be handled separately according to substitution.
An isolated sharp diagnostic band. None of the audited structures contains a nitrile.
A compact exam envelope representing several stretches, not a claim of one experimental normal mode. One or two resolved notches are sufficient.
Supporting evidence above 3000. May be weak or obscured by O-H or N-H.

Include a modest recognizable band in an idealized aldehyde-identification template. It can be weak or undetectable experimentally; must_show is an exam-template choice, not a universal visibility claim.
Optional second member of the characteristic Fermi-resonance pair; may overlap ordinary C-H absorption.
Useful support for cyclohexene. Intensity is symmetry-dependent; do not render every alkene with a carbonyl-strength dip.
One representative ring-stretch band is enough at this grain. Do not mistake it for a strong C=O absorption or draw the complete aromatic fingerprint.
One member of the strong nitro pair; important for nitrobenzene.
Second member of the nitro pair. Interpret the pair together rather than as generic C-O absorption.
Applies to ethanol and propan-1-ol. A strong band in the approximate 1050-1100 exam bin is sufficient; do not copy the experimental multiplet of fingerprint absorptions.
Applies to propan-2-ol. This approximate shift is supporting evidence, not a secure standalone distinction from propan-1-ol.

ir_rules.region: Aryl C-O fingerprint stretching, approximately 1180-1260 cm^-1
ir_rules.note: Supports phenol together with broad O-H and aromatic evidence.
Supporting acid band; the compulsory exam evidence is very broad O-H plus strong C=O.
Strong supporting ester absorption. Position varies with the ester; this is suitable for ethyl acetate.
Optional second representative ester C-O band; do not generate a fingerprint forest.
Flag excludes ester oxygen. C-O alone cannot establish alcohol because ethers and esters also absorb here.

ir_rules.region: Aromatic C-H out-of-plane fingerprint, within 900-675 cm^-1
ir_rules.note: Appropriate supporting band for the monosubstituted benzene derivatives in the audit. Other substitution patterns require different bins.

ir_rules.region: Aromatic C-H out-of-plane fingerprint, within 900-675 cm^-1
ir_rules.note: Optional second prominent band of the usual monosubstituted-benzene pattern.

ir_rules.region: Alkene C-H out-of-plane fingerprint, within 1000-650 cm^-1
ir_rules.note: Suitable coarse support for cyclohexene. Do not apply 700 universally: trans-disubstituted alkenes commonly absorb near 965, and terminal CH2=CH groups near 990 and 910.

ir_rules.region: Taught C-Cl fingerprint bin, approximately 800-600 cm^-1
ir_rules.note: Supporting, environment-dependent evidence only. Do not force this generic position onto every acyl chloride; acetyl chloride identification should prioritize high-frequency C=O and chlorine isotope evidence.
Optional for 1-bromobutane. Bromine isotope evidence in MS is substantially more distinctive than this low-frequency IR band.

observations_from_attached_gifs.ir: The ethanol trace shows a broad O-H trough around 3300, a C-H cluster around 3000-2850, and very strong absorption around 1100-1050 cm^-1. It also contains many smaller fingerprint features, but no strong carbonyl absorption.
observations_from_attached_gifs.hnmr: The displayed spectrum has a methyl triplet near 1.2 ppm, a methylene quartet-like group near 3.7 ppm, and an exchangeable-proton feature near 2.6 ppm. The displayed O-H feature is relatively narrow; it need not be reproduced with that exact shape.
observations_from_attached_gifs.cnmr: Two analyte resonances are visible, approximately 18 and 58 ppm.
observations_from_attached_gifs.ms: The base peak is m/z 31; m/z 45 is substantial and the molecular ion at m/z 46 is clearly visible at roughly one quarter of the base-peak intensity.
observations_from_attached_gifs.limits: The GIFs do not establish solvent identity, acquisition conditions or the origin of every minor feature. No minor band should be confidently labelled as contamination from these images alone.

ir: Broad alcohol O-H near 3300 cm^-1, without acid-like extension through 2500.
Recognizable alkyl C-H absorption near 2900 cm^-1.
Strong representative C-O absorption near 1050-1100 cm^-1.
No C=O dip near 1700; keep the simplified 2000-1500 cm^-1 region flat for ethanol.
hnmr: CH3 triplet near 1.2 ppm, integrating to 3 H.
CH2 quartet near 3.6-3.7 ppm, integrating to 2 H.
One explicitly identified, position-variable O-H signal for the neutral ethanol template.
cnmr: Exactly two ethanol carbon environments, near 18 and 58 ppm.

must_omit: The experimental IR fingerprint forest: retain selected taught support bands, not every bending mode, shoulder and low-frequency trough.

Solvent, reference, water or impurity signals from the analyte-only model unless the question explicitly requests them; do not mistake ethanol's O-H resonance near 2.6 ppm for solvent merely because its position is variable.
Baseline noise, pixel artefacts, drift and instrumental ripples.
Unassigned minor experimental IR features that would falsely suggest a carbonyl or another absent functional group.
Fine NMR structure beyond the intended first-order exam multiplets, including condition-specific O-H coupling and isotope satellites.
rendering_contract: Generate bands from molecular functionality and chemistry; do not fit the Cambridge trace or digitize the SDBS GIF into a curve.
IR axes: transmittance from 0 to 100%, absorptions downward, wavenumber decreasing left to right. A clearly labelled 4000-to-400 or 500 cm^-1 range is suitable.

The ir_rules positions, widths and depths are coarse drawing defaults. must_show=true means retain the feature in the selected idealized exam template when its condition matches; false means optional support, not chemical absence.
Apply carbonyl subtype rules exclusively to each carbonyl group, but allow genuinely separate functional groups to contribute together.
Do not multiply a schematic band depth simply because a SMARTS query returns several equivalent matches.
Use localized, smoothly bounded band profiles and bounded overlap handling. Do not let broad-band tails manufacture absorption in diagnostic regions that should be empty.
For the stated propan-1-ol exam target, the same alcohol pattern applies: O-H around 3300, C-H around 2900, flat 2000-1500 baseline, and strong C-O around 1100.

principles: Predict chemically equivalent proton sets using connectivity, symmetry and the assumed medium; do not create one resonance per hydrogen atom.
Show identifiable chemical-shift regions, multiplicity and integration. Multiplet area, not tallest-line height, represents proton count.
Use n+1 splitting only for appropriate first-order coupling to n equivalent neighbouring protons. It is not a universal rule for aromatic or strongly coupled systems.
Under the usual rapid-exchange exam assumption, O-H does not split adjacent C-H signals and is not itself split by them. Its shift, width and apparent integral are condition-dependent.
Preserve relative line spacings from a common J value, while using enough drawing separation for triplets and quartets to remain readable.
Use a chemical-shift axis in ppm increasing to the left. Exclude solvent and TMS peaks unless requested.

ethanol_worked_example.assumption: Neutral ethanol in an achiral medium with rapid O-H exchange; simplified first-order spectrum.

signals.note: 2.6 ppm is a convenient image-consistent example, not a fixed ethanol identifier or a hard allowable range. D2O exchange removes this signal.

ethanol_worked_example.required_identification: Three proton environments in the idealized neutral-molecule spectrum; nonexchangeable integration ratio 3:2, ideally 3:2:1 including O-H. The 1.2 ppm triplet and 3.6-3.7 ppm quartet establish the characteristic ethyl pattern next to oxygen.
ethanol_worked_example.drawing_note: Triplet and quartet line ratios apply within each multiplet. Normalize their total areas to 3 and 2 respectively rather than using equal overall peak heights.

principles: State the normal exam assumption: broadband proton-decoupled 13C NMR.
Draw one singlet-like line for each chemically distinct carbon environment, respecting molecular symmetry.
Use diagnostic shift regions rather than experimental linewidths or tiny shift differences.
Do not use ordinary 13C peak heights as carbon counts; relaxation and nuclear Overhauser enhancement make them nonquantitative.
Do not apply proton n+1 splitting to a broadband-decoupled 13C spectrum.
Omit solvent, reference peaks, satellites and noise unless explicitly requested.

ethanol_worked_example.required_absences: No carbonyl carbon, aromatic carbon or alkene carbon signals.
ethanol_worked_example.drawing_note: Two clean sticks are enough. Comparable heights are acceptable schematic styling but must not be presented as quantitative integration.

principles: Specify electron-ionization positive-ion MS for this ethanol example. Molecular-ion and fragmentation expectations change with ionization method.
Use a stick spectrum with increasing m/z to the right and relative intensity normalized to a base peak of 100.
Retain a small set of diagnostic ions, the molecular ion when supported, and informative isotope patterns. Do not reproduce every weak experimental stick.
The base peak need not be the molecular ion. For singly charged ions, the molecular-ion nominal m/z corresponds to the molecular nominal mass.
Require chemically plausible ionic formulas and neutral losses. SMILES alone does not determine precise fragment intensities.

For a single chlorine atom, retain approximately 3:1 M:M+2 evidence when the relevant ion is visible; for a single bromine atom, approximately 1:1. Apply these patterns only to ions retaining the halogen.
Do not make a molecular ion mandatory for every compound, or make a dehydration fragment dominant merely because an alcohol is present.

required_peaks.assignment: CH2OH+ is the standard alcohol-fragment assignment; nominal formula CH3O+.
required_peaks.note: Dominant oxygen-containing fragment, commonly explained by alpha cleavage with loss of a methyl radical.
Major fragment visible in the attached spectrum; exact relative height is not an exam requirement.
Clearly identifiable molecular ion, weaker than m/z 31 and 45.

optional_supporting_peaks.assignment: A nominal-mass fragment; C2H5+ is a possible assignment, but unit-mass resolution alone does not exclude isobaric CHO+.

ethanol_worked_example.intensity_policy: These rounded heights summarize the attached GIF for a worked example; they are not universal predictions from ethanol's SMILES.
ethanol_worked_example.isotope_policy: No prominent chlorine- or bromine-like M+2 pair. The small natural-abundance M+1 signal may be omitted at this grain.
ethanol_worked_example.minimum_identifiable_pattern: Base peak 31, major fragment 45, molecular ion 46.

pitfalls.warning: A hydroxy-ketone has both O-H and C=O. Drawing only the ketone band or treating it as a 9701 ketone-only example misrepresents its structure.
pitfalls.action: Accumulate rules for separate functional groups. Reserve a ketone-only IR template for a molecule with no additional diagnostic hydroxyl or other group.

pitfalls.warning: Aldehyde and ketone carbonyl frequencies overlap. Without weak aldehydic C-H near 2720, often accompanied by 2820 cm^-1, IR discrimination is weak.
pitfalls.action: Use a modest aldehydic C-H feature in an idealized identification diagram, but do not treat its experimental absence as proof of a ketone. Seek a 1H NMR aldehyde resonance near 9-10 ppm.

pitfalls.warning: A broad dip at 3300 alone does not distinguish every O-H-containing compound. The acid signature is a much broader 2500-3300 envelope together with C=O.
pitfalls.action: Preserve the different envelope widths and the acid carbonyl; do not create an acid by merely broadening an alcohol band slightly.

pitfalls.warning: Long tails, generic background curves or copied weak experimental structure can create a false 1700 cm^-1 feature in ethanol or propan-1-ol.
pitfalls.action: Keep their simplified 2000-1500 baseline flat. Draw a carbonyl dip only when the molecular structure justifies it.

pitfalls.warning: Omitting all fingerprint information loses useful C-O and out-of-plane evidence; reproducing every fingerprint feature defeats the exam grain.
pitfalls.action: Keep selected taught bands at approximately 1300-1000, 900-675, 1000-650 and 800-600 cm^-1 as applicable, with substitution-aware assignments.

pitfalls.warning: The simplified IR spectra of propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol share the same principal functional-group evidence.
pitfalls.action: Do not promise positional-isomer identification from small C-O shifts. Use 1H and 13C environment counts and splitting.

pitfalls.warning: Phase, concentration, solvent, exchange and instrument conditions affect band widths, O-H shifts and MS intensities.
pitfalls.action: Label values as approximate chemistry-based bins. Preserve diagnostic relationships rather than claiming experimental precision.
